candidate_inference.name: Terminological Carryover Inference
candidate_inference.form: If two source-grounded claims are historically indexed by the same capacity label, that recurrence itself contributes evidence that they support one structurally individuated capacity.

MEM04.label_role: The source record primarily characterizes a past-oriented episodic subsystem; semantic memory appears as a related knowledge-oriented subsystem in a contrast/dependence relation.

CNC05.label_role: The source record directly evaluates architectures for semantic/conceptual knowledge and cross-modal generalization.
CNC05.summary: state-to-outcome dependence in distributed versus shared-convergence architectures

adjudication.reason: The shared label occupies different claim roles and no preserved structural bridge between the two frozen supports is established under either the working basis or CPCG.

preservation_debt_for_unified_capacity_t: Target alignment: justify treating MEM04's related knowledge-oriented subsystem and CNC05's semantic/conceptual architecture as evidence about the same capacity target.
Boundary/granularity alignment: specify how a subsystem distinction in MEM04 maps to an architectural convergence constraint in CNC05.
Preservation map: state which relations must be preserved across the Pi/S/T-centered and K/O/S-centered descriptions.
Rival-representation check: show that the proposed bridge is not an artifact of one chosen representation or explain why a more perspicuous representation is warranted.
Capacity-level warrant: provide independent mechanistic, functional, invariance, or other evidence that licenses the cross-source identity claim.
philosophical_consequence: The procedure changes the status of a label-based capacity thesis from prima facie continuity to an open thesis carrying explicit preservation debt. It neither refutes nor confirms a unified semantic-memory capacity.
inferential_boundary: Post hoc illustrative application; no prevalence or population claim.
